pr_body:
This commit adds support for a `default_transaction_quality_of_service`                     
session setting which when set to `critical`, increases the priority  
of work submitted to admission queues from subsequent SQL requests, 
and when set to `background`, decreases admission queue priority of  
subsequent SQL requests.

This commit also adds a method of controlling the admission queue
priority of internal SQL requests. Now, if InternalExecutor.ExecEx is
called with a nil txn and the InternalExecutorOverride parameter is
passed with a valid QualityOfService setting, the new transaction will
be created with the specified QualityOfService.

This commit adds a `qualityOfService` field to the `activeTxn` in the
[List Sessions API](https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/api/cluster/v2#operation/listSessions).

This commit also includes the current setting of
default_transaction_quality_of_service in the statement bundle built via
EXPLAIN (OPT, ENV).

Fixes #70295

Release note (sql change): Adds session setting 
`default_transaction_quality_of_service` which controls the priority of 
work submitted to the different admission control queues on behalf of 
SQL requests submitted in a session. Admission control must be enabled                                         
for this setting to have an effect, see:
https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v21.2/architecture/admission-control.html
To increase admission control priority of subsequent SQL requests: 
   `SET default_transaction_quality_of_service=critical;` 
To decrease admission control priority of subsequent SQL requests:
   `SET default_transaction_quality_of_service=background;` 
To reset admission control priority to the default session setting 
(in between background and critical):
   `SET default_transaction_quality_of_service=regular;`
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/76512)

There was some discussion in #70295 about when `SET quality_of_service=` would have an effect. I modeled the behavior after `SET default_transaction_read_only=`, which means setting it within an explicit BEGIN/END transaction block would have no effect on that transaction, but it would take effect on subsequent transactions. 

There was also discussion of the `SET TRANSACTION` statement, but it was unclear whether `SET quality_of_service=` should behave as a hybrid between `SET TRANSACTION`, which would take immediate effect on the explicit transaction, and `SET SESSION`, which just affects the value to use the next time a new SQL transaction is created, or if should acts just as a normal `SET SESSION` statement, so I implemented the latter.  But this can be changed if the desired behavior is something else.

> There was also discussion of the SET TRANSACTION statement, but it was unclear whether SET quality_of_service= should behave as a hybrid between SET TRANSACTION, which would take immediate effect on the explicit transaction, and SET SESSION, which just affects the value to use the next time a new SQL transaction is created, or if should acts just as a normal SET SESSION statement, so I implemented the latter. But this can be changed if the desired behavior is something else.

One proposal is that we call this session variable `default_transaction_quality_of_service` and then have a separate `quality_of_service` transaction setting, so you can do `BEGIN; SET TRANSACTION qualit_of_service = 'expedited'; ...; COMMIT;` and have the subsequent transaction observe no effect. This could be nice for applications which share a connection pool and want to only prioritize or deprioritize certain transactions. I suspect it's not much harder. Curious to hear if @vy-ton or others have thoughts.

> I modeled the behavior after SET default_transaction_read_only=, which means setting it within an explicit BEGIN/END transaction block would have no effect on that transaction, but it would take effect on subsequent transactions.

Just to confirm, I would expect to see the setting value has change but it does not take affect?
```
demo@127.0.0.1:26257/movr> show default_transaction_read_only;
  default_transaction_read_only
---------------------------------
  off
(1 row)

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/movr> begin;
BEGIN

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/movr  OPEN> set default_transaction_read_only=on;
SET

demo@127.0.0.1:26257/movr  OPEN> show default_transaction_read_only;
  default_transaction_read_only
---------------------------------
  on
(1 row)
```

> One proposal is that we call this session variable default_transaction_quality_of_service and then have a separate quality_of_service transaction setting, so you can do BEGIN; SET TRANSACTION qualit_of_service = 'expedited'; ...; COMMIT; and have the subsequent transaction observe no effect.

For `transaction_read_only`, there is both `default_transaction_read_only` and `transaction_read_only`. Is this following the pattern that @ajwerner mentioned above? If so, going with this pattern SGTM. It doesnt look like we are consistent, eg `default_transaction_use_follower_reads` doesn't have a matching setting

Just so that it's extra extra explicit, I don't think implementing a variant that allows you to change the priority of the current transaction if you're in a transaction should be in scope for this PR. We should file a follow-up issue for that. I think we should just implement `SET SESSION default_transaction_quality_of_service = ...` here, as that's really darn valuable and leaves the door open to following the pattern established elsewhere for later. I don't think it's even very important to do that in this release. My proposal is about where we should be headed, not what needs to happen for this change.

> I guess there's a reason not to just use something like low, medium and high?

The reason we've been avoiding `LOW`, `NORMAL`, and `HIGH` is because those are the arguments to `SET TRANSACTION PRIORITY` and, well, it's confusing enough that these two concepts exist and are different. 

https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/set-transaction.html#parameters

Random shower thought: `regular` instead of `default`? 

My current favorite triples are: 

1) (`background`, `regular`, `expedited`)
2) (`bronze` /`🥉` , `silver` /`🥈` , `gold`/ `🥇`)  
   * Emoji support would be a fun easter egg
   * `set default_transaction_quality_of_service = '🥇'`, yes please!

Again, defer to @vy-ton as decision maker.

@msirek My preferred triple is `background, regular or normal, top`.  Thoughts?

I did some research on other dbs too:
* [Oracle](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E11882_01/server.112/e24611/apqos_intro.htm#APQOS109) - `highest, high, medium, low`
* [ScyllaDB](https://docs.scylladb.com/using-scylla/workload-prioritization/) - lets you name your own service levels
* [Teradata](https://docs.teradata.com/r/Teradata-VantageTM-Workload-Management-User-Guide/July-2021) - `top, high, medium, low`

+1 to a common theme. I want to encourage users to think about QoS at the higher abstraction of workload/work compared to transaction priorities. Another reason besides naming overlap that I want to avoid `low, normal, high`.

`background, regular, critical` is my final idea. We should ask users to consider what is your background work vs critical work. `best_effort` requires more explanation imo.

issue_context.title: sql: provide mechanism to plumb QoS level into admission control
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The [admission control subsystem] introduced in 21.2 queues work when the system is overloaded. When queuing, the system decides what to admit next based on goals of providing fairness between tenants and providing priority order within a tenant, ultimately with a time-based tie-breaker allowing older work to go first.

When it comes to priority, the space of the current system is 1 byte, and only 3 values are in use: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/util/admission/work_queue.go#L63-L75

At the time of writing, nothing is using `LowPri`, and transactions which hold locks are using `HighPri`. 

In general, when the system is overloaded, some parts of the workload are more important than others. Users may want ways to inform the system of these priority distinctions. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Given the general lack of certainty, this issue proposes that it's best to provide something rather than everything in terms of control. The choice proposed is to expose priority as a session variable. The choice of a session variable was made because of the flexibility it offers. A session variable can be set in the session, from a connection URL, or using database role defaults.

The proposal here is that we introduce a session setting, say, `admission_control_work_priority` or something like that. The value could be an 8bit integer to exactly fit the model inside of the current implementation. Alternatively we could bound the interval to reserve some bits at either end of the spectrum, or we could make it a floating point number which we project into whatever space we use internally. As long as we don't make it `[20, -19]` where 20 is the lowest value, I'm pretty cool with it.

* The meat of this proposal would be to add the new session variable.
     * Add a new session data field [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/sql/sessiondatapb/local_only_session_data.proto#L17-L18).
     * Add an entry here to populate it [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/sql/vars.go#L141-L143)
* Expose some more knobs to, at least, initialize a transaction at a priority level.
     * This would mean updating the constructor [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/kv/txn.go#L134-L137))
     * We may also want to expose a method to update the priority level while a transaction is running. Consider a `SET admission_control_priority = ...` during a transaction.
* Plumb the value from the sessiondata to new transactions.
     * The value will need to be plumbed to transaction [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/sql/txn_state.go#L191).
     * The value will need to be plumbed via [eventTxnStartPayload](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/sql/conn_fsm.go#L101) which will happen [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/sql/conn_executor_exec.go#L1482) or [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/pkg/sql/conn_executor_exec.go#L1502).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Many different approaches have been discussed in the past for how to offer control over priorities. These include

1) Statement fingerprints
2) Application names
3) Users
4) Connection settings

Honestly, we should just do something, and refine it over time.

**Additional context**

The whole thing where we increase the lock strength to `HighPri` may interact in unexpected ways with user-provided priorities. In general, I think it's fine, but we should probably note that once you've laid down a write, you get high priority.

[admission control subsystem]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0fda7519be7d7579526a19f4c9967f2e125d00ba/docs/tech-notes/admission_control.md

Epic CRDB-10353

@RaduBerinde do you think it'd make sense to enforce at the rpc boundary that requests coming from secondary tenants have admission headers with values that fall in this more confined range as a follow-up task?

I am trying to determine the scope of this issue in terms of modifying a currently-running transaction.  I guess what is meant by `Consider a SET admission_control_priority = ... during a transaction` is not the actual use of the `SET` syntax, but a means of doing something, perhaps through an API and not SQL, like:

a. broadcasting out to all nodes in the system a new WorkPriority for a given session and then checking when new work is started on behalf of a transaction belonging to that session. If found, update the priority in the txn's admission header.
  or
b. Something else?

Maybe some discussion on the use case would be helpful, like how the API would be invoked.  Maybe this point is related to support for https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/75840/.  For that, I'm just planning on adding a new field to `sessiondata.InternalExecutorOverride` so that calling InternalExecutor.ExecEx could apply a new priority to a statement execution request. If anything, the way I'd think about it is as having the session variable really be a default for a transaction property. The `SET TRANSACTION` statement can only be the first statement in a transaction. After that, it's not allowed. An example of such a session variable is `default_transaction_read_only`.

One other thought, upon reading this issue again, is if we should remove the word `priority` from the interface altogether and instead use the team `quality_of_service`. The decision to use that terminology came around the same time as I filed the issue.

OK, maybe changing the level of something already running is out of scope, but do you think it is OK for a pre-existing `Txn` to have the priority in its `admissionHeader` changed for a new call to InternalExecutor.ExecEx?  I see `Txn.AdmissionHeader()` already does this for txns that are locking, so I thought it might be OK.  

> The SET TRANSACTION statement can only be the first statement in a transaction. After that, it's not allowed. An example of such a session variable is default_transaction_read_only.

OK, thanks for the pointer about `default_transaction_read_only`. If I understand correctly, if we are doing auto-commits and are not wrapped in a new transaction via a `BEGIN` statement, `SET quality_of_service =` can be issued at any time and has immediate effect on the next statement.  But, if a `BEGIN` has been issued, `SET quality_of_service =` has no effect in the new transaction but it will have an effect in the outer scope once the current transaction is closed via an `END` statement.  For example, setting `default_transaction_read_only = true` within a nested transaction can still affect statements issued after that transaction is closed (t8 can't be created in this case) :
```
root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> SET default_transaction_read_only = false;
SET


Time: 1ms total (execution 0ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> BEGIN;
BEGIN


Time: 0ms total (execution 0ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb  OPEN> values (1);
  column1
-----------
        1
(1 row)


Time: 1ms total (execution 0ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb  OPEN> SET default_transaction_read_only = true;
SET


Time: 1ms total (execution 0ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb  OPEN> create table t7 (a int);
CREATE TABLE


Time: 10ms total (execution 10ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb  OPEN> end;
COMMIT


Time: 18ms total (execution 18ms / network 0ms)

root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> create table t8 (a int);
ERROR: cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction
SQLSTATE: 25006

```
Note: TransactionModes will not be updated with `quality_of_service` as that won't be part of the `SET TRANSACTION` syntax.
